punchline: Two bicycle makers doubted the experts' tables, built a wind tunnel in their shop, and flew.
thirty_sec: In 1901 the Wright brothers' glider lifted less than the published tables predicted. Instead of blaming themselves alone, they built a small wind tunnel in their Dayton bicycle shop and tested wing shapes one by one. Their own measurements shaped the 1902 glider, which flew much better, and powered flight followed in December 1903. McCullough tells it in The Wright Brothers.
